title: EleutherIA: An AI-Powered Scholarly Research Platform for Ancient Philosophy on Free Will
description: EleutherIA is an open scholarly research platform and FAIR-aligned knowledge graph for ancient debates on free will, fate, moral responsibility, and agency across the Greco-Roman and early Christian worlds. This archive combines a curated knowledge graph, an ancient-text corpus, and an agentic GraphRAG stack for citation-grounded question answering, graph exploration, and data quality auditing. As of the 2026-06-05 KG snapshot bundled with this release, the graph contains 20,060 nodes, 56,737 edges, and 19,751 passage citations over 241 ancient works and roughly 17,800 anchored passages in Greek and Latin (with English translations); the RDF export carries 560,110 triples with per-edge provenance reification and a VoID/DCAT dataset description aligned on CIDOC-CRM, FOAF, SKOS, Dublin Core, PROV-O, and BIBO. Coverage spans roughly twelve centuries, from the Presocratics and Classical Greek philosophy through Hellenistic, Roman Imperial, Patristic, and Late Antique authors, while also linking ancient primary sources to modern scholarship and reception history. Version 5.1.0 adds enforced answer-time verification: a deterministic quote-fidelity gate that verifies every quoted ancient-language span verbatim against the cited passage, a corpus-backed ancient-text verifier, an adversarial per-claim citation auditor (CitationVerifierV2), a golden evaluation harness running in CI (citation precision/recall gold and a fabrication must-never-appear suite, both derived from the project's manual integrity audits), corpus tamper-evidence (per-passage SHA-256 and edition provenance), and a unified item-by-item integrity review queue. All statistics are machine-generated from the dataset snapshots (scripts/gen_stats.py, data/stats.json). The repository includes the application code, database migrations, ingestion and repair scripts, evaluation reports, and documentation needed to reproduce, inspect, and extend the archive.
